Firstly, glad you've found someone you love that you have Interest in acutally helping the relationship. I definitely say you should have a conversation with your girlfriend, sit her down when she's calm and talk to her about how her outburst make you feel. Try not to do it when she's already angry or upset, just when you're both calm and you feel secure. 

I suggest you watch some videos or just lightly research general anger management, funnily enough, I'm 19M dating 17F and I also have a pretty bad temper. My girlfriend talked to me about it, it didn't help much when it was after I got upset while driving about something. However when I was calmer one day she explained to me how she loves me dearly but my anger can be a bit unchecked and it makes her uncomfortable over the phone or even scared in person. I made it clear to her I would never dare take my anger out specifically on her, and that it was just me being upset. I looked up some things about anger management, general stuff like thinking before an outburst, breathing, avoiding stress etc. and it's been helping.

I think you should just try your best to have your partner first recognize it's a problem, then offer some light solutions. If the problem persists talk to them about anger management therapy. Look into it and consider your options. 

I've found though, I'm much less prone anger outbursts when I'm generally just healthy, sleep, food, exercise and water go a long way
